content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the stages of labour and birth
Explain the role of hormones in birth
Describe what happens immediately after birth

(parturition) is the process by which the baby leaves the uterus. It typically occurs around 40 weeks after fertilisation. Birth involves powerful uterine contractions controlled by hormones, and occurs in three stages.
Throughout pregnancy: progesterone high, prevents contractions
Near birth: progesterone drops, oestrogen rises
Uterus becomes more sensitive to oxytocin
Unlike most body processes (negative feedback), birth uses positive feedback - the response amplifies the stimulus.
Must reach 10 cm for baby's head
No longer receiving oxygen via placenta
Stump dries and falls off (~1-2 weeks)
Surgical incision through abdomen and uterus
Special care baby unit (SCBU) or neonatal intensive care (NICU)
It can happen at various times during labour
Birth is always painful without medical intervention
Pain varies; various pain relief options available
In birth, it's essential and self-limiting (ends at delivery)
Cutting the umbilical cord hurts the baby
There are no nerve endings in the cord
Birth triggered by hormonal changes (progesterone drops, oxytocin rises)
Stage 1: Cervix dilates to 10 cm (6-12 hours)
Stage 2: Baby delivered through birth canal (20 min-2 hours)
Baby takes first breath when cord is cut
Oxytocin also involved in breastfeeding and bonding
